notes: NCBI StatPearls Spinal Cord Subacute Combined Degeneration was reread for posterior/lateral column demyelination and the B12-deficiency clinical phenotype.
NCBI Vitamin B12 Deficiency was reread for methylmalonic-acid accumulation and myelin injury involving dorsal columns, lateral corticospinal and sometimes spinocerebellar/peripheral pathways.
PubMed clinical/MRI study was reread for posterior-column dysfunction and central motor-pathway involvement.
The official USMLE 2026 nervous-system domain was verified for spinal-cord localization and metabolic/nutritional neurologic disease.

blueprint.system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

duplicate_gate.diagnosis: Subacute combined degeneration due to vitamin B12 deficiency

claim_audit.localization: SCD classically affects posterior/dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts.
claim_audit.posterior_column_signs: Loss of vibration/proprioception and positive Romberg localize to dorsal columns/sensory pathways.
claim_audit.corticospinal_signs: Hyperreflexia, clonus and extensor plantar responses localize to corticospinal upper-motor-neuron pathways.
claim_audit.b12_context: Autoimmune gastritis is a recognized cause of vitamin B12 deficiency; elevated methylmalonic acid supports cellular B12 deficiency.
claim_audit.other_tracts_nuance: Spinocerebellar and peripheral-nerve involvement can occur, so the item asks for the pair best explaining the supplied exam rather than claiming exclusive anatomic involvement.
claim_audit.distractor_checks: Anterior horn, spinothalamic, autonomic intermediolateral and isolated spinocerebellar patterns do not simultaneously explain proprioceptive loss plus UMN signs.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: The patient has biochemical B12 deficiency and simultaneous sensory ataxia from impaired vibration/proprioception plus corticospinal UMN signs. That is the defining 'combined' dorsal-column/lateral-corticospinal localization.
adversarial_second_pass.tabes_challenge: Tabes dorsalis can damage posterior columns and cause sensory ataxia, but it does not produce the bilateral corticospinal hyperreflexia/Babinski pattern and the B12 biochemical context is explicit.
adversarial_second_pass.copper_deficiency_challenge: Copper deficiency can phenocopy SCD anatomically. The item does not ask the etiologic differential; it provides confirmed B12 deficiency and asks tract localization, so the correct pair remains unchanged.
adversarial_second_pass.nitrous_oxide_challenge: Nitrous oxide can functionally inactivate cobalamin and cause the same tract syndrome; no exposure is provided and again this would not change the anatomic answer.
adversarial_second_pass.peripheral_neuropathy_challenge: B12 deficiency can cause peripheral neuropathy, which might reduce reflexes. The supplied hyperreflexia/clonus/Babinski specifically demonstrates dominant central corticospinal involvement.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All options are tract pairs of comparable neuroanatomic specificity; the key is not uniquely phrased.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No serum B12 threshold, MMA cutoff, MRI sensitivity, or recovery timeline is required.
